sanskrit: vaiśvānaraḥ saṃ tapaty antarikṣaṃ divaṃ ca samiddho agnir divyas tapojāḥ | śikṣantv asmā abhi sunvanti soma ṛtena bhrājann amṛtaṃ vaste atkī ||
english: Vaiśvānara burns together the atmosphere and heaven; the divine fire, blazing, born of fervent heat. May they render service to him — they who press the soma; shining by sacred order (ṛta), he clothes himself in immortality as a garment.

sanskrit: rārahyete nelayataḥ śītarūre tanvāv asya bhīme | rūpāṇy eti bahudhā vasāno guhā kṛṇvānas tanvaḥ parācīḥ ||
english: The two awe-inspiring forms of him — the cold and the hot — gleam and do not rest. He goes about assuming many forms, robing himself in diverse shapes, concealing his bodies in secret, turning them away to remote places.

sanskrit: pañcāre cakre parivartamāne samārohanti bhuvanāni viśvā | tasya nākṣas tapyate bhūribhāraḥ sanād eva na chidyate sanābhiḥ ||
english: Upon the five-spoked wheel revolving, all the worlds mount together. Its axle, bearing the immense burden, grows hot; from of old it is never severed together with its hub.

sanskrit: pañcabhis taptas tapaty eṣa etat sahasradhāmānam anu tiṣṭhanty enam | sapta tvā sūrya harito vahanti brahmaṇādityas trivṛtā mukhena ||
english: Heated by the five, he burns in turn; they attend upon him of a thousand abodes. The seven bay mares draw thee, O Sūrya; Āditya, with Brahman, with the triple-twined mouth.

sanskrit: vi dyotate dyotata ā ca dyotate apsv antar amṛto gharma udyan | hantā vṛtrasya haritām anīkam anādhṛṣṭās tanvaḥ sūryasya ||
english: He flashes apart, he flashes, and he flashes back — the immortal Gharma (heat-vessel) rising within the waters. The slayer of Vṛtra, the host of the bay ones, the bodies of Sūrya — unassailable.

sanskrit: gharmaḥ paścād uta gharmaḥ purastād ayodaṃṣṭrāya dviṣato 'pi dadhmaḥ | vaiśvānaraḥ śītarūre vasānaḥ sapatnān me dviṣato hantu sarvān ||
english: The Gharma from behind and the Gharma from before — we set them against the iron-fanged foe who hates us. Vaiśvānara, robing himself in cold and in heat, let him smite all my rivals who bear enmity toward me.

sanskrit: ṛtūn ṛtubhiḥ śrapayati brahmaṇaikavīro gharmaḥ śucānaḥ samidhā samiddhaḥ | brahmā tvā tapati brahmaṇā tejasā ca ||
english: He cooks the seasons by means of the seasons; the Gharma, the solitary hero of Brahman, purified, kindled with sacrificial fuel. The Brahmin sacrificer heats thee with sacred formula and with fiery splendour.

sanskrit: brahma jajñānaṃ prathamaṃ samā dade taj jāyamānaṃ na bibhide na bhidyate | tad aṅgamānaṃ pitaraṃ vyāhati tasya nāḍya ātatā vitatās tatā u tāḥ ||
english: Brahman (the sacred power), born first, was taken together — that which is coming into being was not split apart and is not split. That which moves in the limbs speaks to the father; its veins are stretched out, spread wide — stretched indeed are they.

sanskrit: asayajjāna sata ā jabhāra ya īṃ jajāna sa id asya bhartā | prajāpatiḥ prajābhiḥ saṃvidānas trīṇi jyotīṃṣi dadhate na pākaḥ ||
english: From the existent he bore away that which was unborn; he who begot it — he indeed is its sustainer. Prajāpati, coming to understanding with his creatures, holds the three lights — the immature one does not.

sanskrit: prajāpatiś carati garbhe antaḥ sa jāyamāno bahudhā pra jāyate | tasya padam abhi paśyanti vedhasas tasminn ārpitā bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: Prajāpati moves within the womb; being born, he is born manifold. The wise (vedhas) behold his footstep; upon him all the worlds are strung.

sanskrit: yasmin devāḥ pitaro manuṣyā arā nābhāv iva śritāḥ | apāṃ tvā puṣpaṃ pṛcchāmi yatra tan māyayāhitam ||
english: In whom gods, ancestors, and men are rested like spokes at the hub — thee, the flower of the waters, I ask: where is it deposited by māyā (creative power)?

sanskrit: yatrāpāṃ puṣpaṃ nihitaṃ māyayātihitaṃ guhā | yo vai tad vidyāt pratyakṣaṃ sa vidyād brāhmaṇaṃ mahat ||
english: Where the flower of the waters is placed, set exceedingly by māyā in a hidden place — he who would know that directly, he would know the great Brahman.

sanskrit: maṇis triṣūtro nihitaḥ svarvid ūrdhvas tiryaṅ viśa etu prajānan | sa pumān puṃso janayann ṛtena sarvān antān gacchatu sadya eva ||
english: The jewel threaded on three (threads), set in place, the heaven-knower — upright, across-turned, may it enter, being aware. That virile one, generating from the man by sacred order, let him reach all the ends straightway.

sanskrit: sarvāṃ rātrīṃ sam oṣatv ādityo jātavedasā | agner adhi divam ā rohann āyuṣā sam anaktu mā varcasā saṃ sṛjāti mā ||
english: May Āditya wholly burn through the entire night together with Jātavedas (fire). Mounting up to heaven above the fire, let him anoint me with life-span; may he unite me with vital lustre (varcas).

sanskrit: gharmaḥ sāhasraḥ samidhā samiddho 'sapatnāḥ pradiśo me kṛṇotu | sapatnān sarvān me sūryo hantu vaiśvānaro hariḥ ||
english: The Gharma of a thousand (fires), kindled with sacrificial fuel — let it make the quarters of the sky free of rivals for me. Let Sūrya, Vaiśvānara, the tawny one, smite all my rivals.

sanskrit: gharmas taptaḥ pra dahatu bhrātṛvyān dviṣato mama | ā dattāṃ chatrūn āditya udyan sūryaḥ pṛtanyataḥ ||
english: The Gharma, made hot, let it utterly burn the rivals, those who hate me. Let Āditya, Sūrya rising, give over to (our keeping) the enemies who wage battle.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaraḥ pra dahatu bhrātṛvyān dviṣato vṛṣā | udyan me śukra ādityo vi mṛdho hantu sūryaḥ ||
english: Vaiśvānara the bull, let him utterly burn the rivals, those who hate (me). The brilliant Āditya rising, Sūrya — let him crush and smite my adversaries.

sanskrit: śukraṃ suparṇaṃ hari brahma bhrājad ajasraṃ jyotir divam ā tatāna | hariḥ suparṇaḥ pramathiṣṇur āśuḥ sapatnān hantu mahātā vadhena ||
english: The brilliant, fair-winged, tawny Brahman — the unfailing, shining light stretched out through heaven. The tawny fair-winged one, swift, ever ready to smite — let him strike down rivals with his great weapon.

sanskrit: hariḥ suparṇaḥ sudino 'bhayaṃkaro hiraṇyavarṇo durudāpa āśuḥ | sapatnān sarvān me sūrya ādityo hantu raśmibhiḥ ||
english: The tawny fair-winged one, bringer of fair days, maker of fearlessness, of golden hue, hard to overcome, swift — Sūrya, Āditya, let him smite all my rivals with his rays.

sanskrit: mahāntam arthaṃ pari sadya etv ahorātre vidadhac chukra udyan | sapatnān sarvān me sūrya etu vaiśvānaro dahan ||
english: Let him straightway encompass the great goal — the brilliant one rising, distributing day and night. Let Sūrya, Vaiśvānara burning, go against all my rivals.

sanskrit: udyann adya mitramaha ity ekā ||
english: "Rising today, O great Mitra" — thus (goes) the one (verse, cited by incipit).

sanskrit: tejas tapāṃsi mukhato bibharṣy ānandaṃ bhūtiṃ mahasaḥ pratiṣṭhām | paryūhamāṇaḥ śriyam eṣi sarvato amoghaṃ satyaṃ yaśa udyataṃ te ||
english: You bear fiery splendour and austerities before your face; bliss, prosperity, and the standing-ground of greatness. Moving all around, you go toward glory from every side — unfailing, true is the fame raised aloft that is yours.

sanskrit: brahmacārīṣṇaṃś carati rodasī ubhe yasmin devāḥ saṃmanaso bhavanti | sa dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyām utāmūṃ sa ācāryaṃ tapasā pipartu ||
english: The fiery brahmacārin (student of sacred knowledge) moves through both worlds, the earth and heaven; in him the gods become of one mind. He upheld this earth and yonder heaven — let him by austerity sustain the teacher.

sanskrit: ācārya upanayamāno brahmacāriṇaṃ kṛṇute garbham antaḥ | taṃ rātrīs tisra udare bibharti taṃ jātaṃ draṣṭum abhisaṃyanti devāḥ | brahmacāriṇaṃ pitaro manuṣyā devajanā gandharvā enam anu yanti sarve ||
english: The teacher, initiating the brahmacārin, makes him an embryo within. Three nights he carries him in his belly; the gods come together to behold him when born. The ancestors, men, divine beings, and gandharvas — all of them follow after this brahmacārin.

sanskrit: trayastriṃśataṃ triśatān ṣaṭ sahasrān sarvān sa devāṃs tapasā piparti | iyaṃ samit pṛthivī dyaur dvitīyā- -utāntarikṣaṃ samidhā pṛṇāti | brahmacārī samidhā mekhalāvī śrameṇa lokāṃs tapasā piparti ||
english: He nourishes by austerity all the gods — the thirty-three, the three hundred, the six thousand. This earth is (his) fuel-stick, heaven the second — and the atmosphere he fills with sacrificial fuel. The brahmacārin, fuel-laden, girded with the sacred cord, nourishes the worlds by toil and by austerity.

sanskrit: pūrvo jāto brahmaṇo brahmacārī gharmaṃ vasānas tapaso 'dhi tiṣṭhat | tasmāj jātaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ brahma jyeṣṭhaṃ devāś ca sarve amṛtena sākam ||
english: Born first of Brahman, the brahmacārin, robing himself in the Gharma (heat), stood supreme over austerity. From him was born the brahmaṇa, the eldest Brahman — and all the gods together with immortality.

sanskrit: brahmacārī samidhā samiddhaḥ kārṣṇaṃ vasāno dīkṣito dīrghaśmaśruḥ | sa sadya eti pūrvād aparaṃ samudraṃ lokān saṃrabhya muhur ācarikrat ||
english: The brahmacārin, kindled with sacrificial fuel, wearing a black antelope skin, consecrated (dīkṣita), long-bearded — he goes straightway from the eastern to the western ocean, grasping the worlds, roaming about repeatedly.

sanskrit: brahmacārī janayan brahma- -apo lokaṃ prajāpatiṃ parameṣṭhiṇaṃ virājam | garbho bhūtvāmṛtasya yonāv indro bhūtvāsurāṃs tatarha ||
english: The brahmacārin generating Brahman, the waters, the world, Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, and Virāj — having become an embryo in the womb of immortality, having become Indra, he crushed the asuras.

sanskrit: imāṃ bhūmīṃ pṛthivīṃ brahmacārī bhikṣāṃ jabhāra prathamo divaṃ ca | te brahma kṛtvā samidhā upāsate tayor ārpitā bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: The brahmacārin, first of all, bore alms from this earth and from heaven. They who make Brahman and tend the (sacred fire) with fuel — upon those two all the worlds are strung.

sanskrit: ācāryas tatakṣa nabhasī ubhe urvī gambhīre pṛthivīṃ divaṃ ca | te brahmacārī tapasābhi rakṣati tayor devāḥ sadhamādaṃ madanti ||
english: The teacher fashioned the two firmaments — the two vast, deep (spaces) — the earth and the heaven. The brahmacārin guards both of them with austerity; upon those two the gods rejoice together in exhilaration.

sanskrit: arvāg anyaḥ paro anyo guhā nidhī nihitau brāhmaṇasya | tau brahmacārī tapasābhi rakṣati tat kevalaṃ kṛṇute brahma vidvān ||
english: One (treasure) is this side, another is beyond — two hidden hoards set in the hidden place of the brahmaṇa. The brahmacārin guards both of them with austerity; the one who knows makes that Brahman entire and sole.
